extracted.intended_audience: Patent examiners and other IP Australia staff; also patent attorneys/agents and applicants seeking to understand examination practice
extracted.subtask_description: Official examination manual for handling patent examination at IP Australia covering dates, standards (novelty, inventive/innovative step), sufficiency/support, patentable subject-matter, procedures for acceptance/refusal, divisional and special application types, and related processes (PSO, re-examination, innovation patents, prohibition orders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority dates and Filing Dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of priority dates and filing dates relevant to examination and entitlement issues (section 5.6.1.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes determining which dates apply for novelty, inventive step and priority entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Publication
rubrics_metrics.description: How publication of documents affects examination and what constitutes prior art (section 5.6.1.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers consequences of publication timing for novelty/whole-of-contents objections and public availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Invention, Alleged Invention, Meaning of a Document etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authoritative definitions used during examination to interpret claims and cited documents (section 5.6.1.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides construction of terms such as 'invention' and 'document' when assessing patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of Probabilities Standard (and its application in examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard of proof applied in examination is the balance of probabilities and how it is to be applied (sections 5.6.1.4–5.6.1.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how examiners weigh evidence and make findings on issues like priority, entitlement, and enablement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and substantive considerations when a request for examination is made (section 5.6.2.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes prerequisites and what to verify before commencing substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application in a State of Lapse?
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations when an application may already be lapsed before or at time of examination (section 5.6.2.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for examiners on identifying lapse and consequences for proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of Time Requests (Section 223 considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to assess requests for extension of time under section 223 and related actions (section 5.6.2.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes treatment of s223 applications, common deficiencies, discretionary matters and advertising of extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification and consequences of fee payment (section 5.6.2.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers excess claim fees, invitations to pay, refunds and fee-related processing prior to examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations of Specifications and Article 19/34 Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for translations, certification and handling poor translations for examination (section 5.6.2.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes verification of translation certification and related annex on verification of translation letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining Priority Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and checks for obtaining priority documents necessary for examination (section 5.6.2.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on when and how to obtain certified priority documents for assessing priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report Dispatch, Correction of Report etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative matters concerning dispatching examination reports and correcting reports (section 5.6.2.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes handling further report considerations and corrections after dispatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convention Applications and Related Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues specific to convention applications relevant to commencement and conduct of examination (section 5.6.2.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers cross-border priority and related procedural points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Amendments Made Prior to Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat amendments filed before substantive examination begins (section 5.6.3.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must determine whether amendments change scope/entitlement and whether they are allowable before examining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims are directed to a Single Invention (Unity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of unity — whether the claims are directed to a single inventive concept (section 5.6.3.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for identifying lack of unity and implications for search/examination coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omnibus Claims – References to the Description or Drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment and validity of omnibus claims that refer to the description or drawings (section 5.6.3.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines the acceptability and limits of omnibus-style claim drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Specifications – Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: How provisional specifications are to be handled when the complete application reaches examination (section 5.6.3.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes what to examine from a provisional filing and how it affects complete specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art – What is Included (Publicly Available, Exclusions, Grace Period)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and scope of prior art for novelty/inventive step including statutory exclusions and grace periods (section 5.6.4.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists what constitutes prior art, exclusions (e.g. statutory), and how grace periods operate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construing a Citation
rubrics_metrics.description: How to interpret and construe a cited document when considering relevance (section 5.6.4.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on reading citations in context and determining disclosed subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of Disclosure Required (Enabling Disclosure, Clear and Unmistakable Directions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for when a cited document discloses subject-matter sufficiently to defeat novelty or support combinations (section 5.6.4.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains enabling disclosure requirements and when directions are clear/unmistakable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Source of Information and Combination of Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When a single document is sufficient versus when documents may be combined as prior art (section 5.6.4.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes tests for combining documents and determining single-source status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third Party Notifications and Identifying/Raising Citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for third party notifications and examiner practice for identifying and raising citations (sections 5.6.4.5–5.6.4.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers when to notify applicants and how to present citations in reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach to assessing novelty of claimed subject-matter (section 5.6.5.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes consideration of whole-of-contents objections and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole of Contents Objection
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the 'whole of contents' basis to object to claims for lack of novelty or sufficiency (section 5.6.5.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the doctrine and its application in examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Use, Secret Use and Confidential Information
rubrics_metrics.description: How evidence of prior use, secret use or confidential disclosures affects novelty/entitlement (section 5.6.5.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on assessing and proving prior use and secret/confidential information issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty – Specific Examples and Selections (including chemical selection issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Worked examples for novelty objections, selection inventions and issues specific to chemical compositions (sections 5.6.5.4–5.6.5.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex and examples illustrate application of novelty principles to chemical/selection cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive Step Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory and practice requirements for inventive step (section 5.6.6.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out the basic legal tests and the types of findings examiners must make.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information for Assessing Inventive Step
rubrics_metrics.description: What information (prior art, common general knowledge etc.) should be considered when assessing inventive step (section 5.6.6.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists sources and evidence examiners should use in inventive step analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests for Inventive Step
rubrics_metrics.description: The various tests used to determine inventive step (section 5.6.6.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes approach to identifying the person skilled in the art, the common general knowledge, and formulating the technical problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing Inventive Step (including indicators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical approach to assessing inventive step and indicators that support or undermine it (sections 5.6.6.4–5.6.6.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for step-by-step assessment and common indicators (unexpected result, long-felt need, commercial success noted where relevant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive Step Issues Specific to Chemical Compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular considerations for inventive step when chemical compositions or related claims are involved (section 5.6.6.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples specific to chemistry and how tests may be applied differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims are Clear and Succinct
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that claims be clear and succinct as part of s40 and claim construction (section 5.6.7.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must object where claims are ambiguous, vague, or overly prolix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and Complete Disclosure – s40(2)(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement for the specification to disclose the invention clearly and completely as required by s40(2)(a) (section 5.6.7.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner assesses whether the disclosure enables a person skilled in the art to perform the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for the Claims – s40(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the specification provides support for the claims under s40(3) (section 5.6.7.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides examiners in determining whether claim scope is fairly based on the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference Between 'Clear and Complete Disclosure' and 'Support'
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between enablement (clear and complete disclosure) and claim support/fair basis (section 5.6.7.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains different legal questions and tests for these two requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Method
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligation to disclose the best method known to the inventor for performing the invention (section 5.6.7.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner considers whether the specification omits known superior methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete Disclosure for Micro-Organisms and Other Life Forms (Budapest Treaty, Deposits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special requirements for biological materials including deposit requirements and Budapest Treaty considerations (section 5.6.7.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on when deposit is necessary and how to treat sequence/bio disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Define the Invention / Claims are Fairly Based
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle that claims must define the invention and be fairly based on the disclosure (sections 5.6.7.7 and 5.6.7.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes sub-tests for fair basis and discussion of alternatives, claiming by results, reach-through claims, and related points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Eligible Subject Matter (Manner of Manufacture) – General Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Framework for assessing whether subject-matter is a 'manner of manufacture' and therefore patent-eligible (section 5.6.8.1 and following).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out high-level approach and legal tests for patentable subject-matter under Australian law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions and Specific Subject-Matter Issues (discoveries, scientific theories, printed matter, mere working directions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of subject-matter commonly treated as excluded from patentability (sections 5.6.8.3–5.6.8.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on identifying non-patentable categories such as mere discoveries, abstract ideas, and non-technical subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer-Implemented Inventions, Schemes and Business Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: How to assess computer-implemented inventions, schemes and business methods under manner of manufacture (section 5.6.8.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific considerations distinguishing technical contribution from mere implementation of a scheme on a computer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Algorithms and Games/Gaming Machines
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of mathematical algorithms and games/gaming machines for patent eligibility (sections 5.6.8.8 and 5.6.8.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner guidance on when such subject-matter may be excluded or, in narrow circumstances, patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological Materials, Nucleic Acids, Micro-Organisms, and Human Beings
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of nucleic acids, genetic information, microorganisms, life forms and issues concerning human beings/biological processes (sections 5.6.8.11–5.6.8.15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes discussion of ethical/legal limits and deposit/support requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinations, Collocations, Kits, Packages and Mere Admixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: How combinations and mere admixtures are treated for patent eligibility and inventive step (section 5.6.8.16).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must assess whether the combination produces a new technical effect or is merely a juxtaposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Uses and Utility (Usefulness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of new uses and whether claimed inventions meet the utility/usefulness requirement (sections 5.6.8.17–5.6.8.19).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on establishing utility and new use claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and Time for Acceptance, Postponement and Revocation of Acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and substantive conditions for acceptance and timing, postponement, revocation and related matters (sections 5.6.9.1–5.6.9.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes grounds and timeframes for acceptance, postponement, extension and revocation of acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal of Acceptance / Refusal of an Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances and specific circumstances that lead to refusal of acceptance or refusal of grant (sections 5.6.9.5–5.6.9.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on notice, reasons and procedures where applications are refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued Examination, Lapsing and Withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Consequences and procedure where examination continues, or where applications lapse or are withdrawn (sections 5.6.9.7–5.6.9.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains options and record-keeping where prosecution continues or application lapses/withdraws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double Patenting and Parallel Applications (multiple applications & innovation/standard applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues of double patenting and handling parallel applications claiming the same subject-matter (sections 5.6.9.10–5.6.9.11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes treatment of applications filed for innovation vs standard patents and decisions to prevent double patenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional Applications – Requirements and Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements to claim divisional status, priority entitlement, time limits for filing and examination of divisional applications (section 5.6.10 and sub-sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers procedural outline for divisional examination and status of the parent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents of Addition – Conditions and Differentiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions for filing patents of addition, how they differ from parent applications and examination considerations (section 5.6.11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner guidance on improvement/modification claims and interplay with parent patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Search and Opinion (PSO) – Requests and Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Office procedure for preliminary search and opinion requests, how the PSO is conducted and the report requirements (sections 5.6.12.1–5.6.12.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes format/contents of PSO report and response handling (section 5.6.12.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-Examination – Process and Completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Commencement, process and completion criteria for re-examination of an application (sections 5.6.13.1–5.6.13.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes outcomes such as refusal to grant or revocation following re-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition Orders and Applications Concerning Defence/Associated Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling of applications subject to prohibition orders (e.g. defence-related/associated technology) and their effect (section 5.6.14 and sub-sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details when applications are prohibited, effect of orders, and special processing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation Patents – System, Formalities and Innovative Step
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination and formal requirements for innovation patents including determining innovative step, certification, opposition and expiry (sections 5.6.15.1–5.6.15.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes special annex (certification form) and procedural differences from standard patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annexes and Procedural Outlines (Full Examination, National Phase, PSO etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of annexes (procedural outlines, examples, checklists and forms) to guide examination practice (multiple annex references throughout 5.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should use annexes such as Procedural Outline for Full Examination, Indicators of Special Considerations for national phase, and example letters/forms to ensure consistent practice.
